extracted.intended_audience: exporters, regulated parties (BIS licensees), pesticide registrants, and legal practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register notices that (1) amend pesticide-residue tolerance tables and specify compliance measurement rules, and (2) issue BIS Orders denying export privileges under ECRA—setting statutory basis, prohibited conduct, scope, appeal rights, and effective durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory basis for denial (ECRA §1760(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to Section 1760(e) of the Export Control Reform Act (ECRA), the export privileges of any person who has been convicted of certain offenses (including, but not limited to, 18 U.S.C. 371) may be denied for a period of up to ten (10) years from the date of his/her conviction. 50 U.S.C. 4819(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites ECRA as enacted Aug 13, 2018 (codified at 50 U.S.C. 4801-4852). This is the statutory authority for issuance of denial orders; the maximum denial period is up to ten years measured from the conviction date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of BIS-issued licenses in which the convicted person had an interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) licenses or other authorizations issued under ECRA in which the person had an interest at the time of the conviction may be revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice states BIS will revoke licenses in which the Denied Person had an interest at time of conviction. Applied as part of the denial remedy to remove existing export authorizations tied to the convicted person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity for written submission under 15 CFR 766.25
rubrics_metrics.description: As provided in Section 766.25 of the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), BIS provides notice and opportunity for the convicted person to make a written submission to BIS. Failure to submit is noted in the administrative record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement: BIS must provide notice and opportunity to respond (written submission). The record may reflect whether BIS received a submission; absence of a submission is a stated factual basis for proceeding with the denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of prohibited activities for the Denied Person
rubrics_metrics.description: From the effective date of the Order the Denied Person may not directly or indirectly participate in any way in any transaction involving any commodity, software or technology exported or to be exported from the United States that is subject to the Regulations, including but not limited to: (A) applying for, obtaining, or using any license, license exception, or export control document; (B) carrying on negotiations concerning, or ordering, buying, receiving, using, selling, delivering, storing, disposing of, forwarding, transporting, financing, or otherwise servicing in any way, any transaction involving any item subject to the Regulations; or (C) benefitting in any way from any transaction involving any item subject to the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long, non-exhaustive list of activities that Denied Person is barred from engaging in directly or indirectly; 'participate in any way' is broad—applies to acts that would use or access export-controlled items or authorizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions on others interacting with the Denied Person (third-party restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person may, directly or indirectly, (A) export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) to or on behalf of the Denied Person any item subject to the Regulations; (B) take any action that facilitates the acquisition or attempted acquisition by the Denied Person of ownership, possession, or control of any item subject to the Regulations that has been or will be exported from the United States (including financing or other support); (C) take any action to acquire from or to facilitate acquisition from the Denied Person any item subject to the Regulations that has been exported from the United States; (D) obtain from the Denied Person in the United States any item subject to the Regulations with knowledge or reason to know that the item will be, or is intended to be, exported from the United States; or (E) engage in any transaction to service any item subject to the Regulations that has been or will be exported and which is owned, possessed, or controlled by the Denied Person, or service any item of whatever origin that is owned, possessed or controlled by the Denied Person if such service involves the use of any item subject to the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Servicing' is defined for purposes of paragraph (E) to mean installation, maintenance, repair, modification or testing. These prohibitions impose affirmative obligations on third parties to avoid dealings that would facilitate the Denied Person’s access to regulated items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to extend Order to related persons to prevent evasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to ECRA §1760(e) and EAR §§766.23 and 766.25, any other person, firm, corporation, or business organization related to the Denied Person by ownership, control, position of responsibility, affiliation, or other connection in the conduct of trade or business may also be made subject to the provisions of the Order in order to prevent evasion of the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency may target affiliates, successors, assigns, employees, agents, representatives, or other related entities where there is a risk of evasion—based on ownership/control/affiliation or conduct of business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and procedure (Part 756)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with Part 756 of the Regulations, the Denied Person may file an appeal of the Order with the Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security. The appeal must be filed within 45 days from the date of the Order and must comply with the provisions of Part 756 of the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies a 45-day filing deadline and incorporates procedural requirements of 15 CFR Part 756 for appeals of denial orders; failure to meet Part 756 requirements could affect appeal consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order delivery and publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the Order shall be delivered to the Denied Person and shall be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative due-process and public-notice practice: orders are both served on the individual and made public via Federal Register publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and duration of Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order is effective immediately upon issuance and shall remain in effect until the specified date (example entries: until April 17, 2034; until May 23, 2030; until March 1, 2033; etc., depending on the conviction date and denial period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial periods are calculated from the date of conviction and may be for the statutory maximum (up to 10 years) or for a shorter period; Orders state the precise expiration date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of pesticide residue tolerances and measurement rule (parent compound only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolerances are established for residues of specified pesticide active ingredients (including metabolites and degradates) in or on the listed commodities. Compliance with the tolerance levels specified in the applicable Table is to be determined by measuring only the named parent compound (e.g., 'measuring only famoxadone (5-methyl-5-(4-phenoxyphenyl)-3-(phenylamino)-2,4-oxazolidinedione) in or on the commodity').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For several listed pesticides (famoxadone, flutolanil, isoxaflutole, aminopyralid, fenazaquin, tembotrione, etc.), the rule text explicitly states that only the parent compound is to be measured for compliance. Tables list parts-per-million tolerances by commodity; revisions involve adding table headings and revising specific commodity entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional registration tolerances (regional tolerances defined by §180.1(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolerances with a regional registration as defined in §180.1(1) are established for residues of the fungicide (or pesticide) in or on the commodities listed in the designated Table. Compliance with the tolerance levels specified in the Table is to be determined by measuring only the parent compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule distinguishes national tolerances from those with 'regional registration' status; regional tolerances are explicitly established by table and measured by parent compound only. Cross-reference to §180.1(1) for the definition of regional registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commodity-by-commodity parts-per-million tolerance tables and procedural table edits
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulatory text uses tables (e.g., 'Table 1 to Paragraph (a)', 'Table 2 to Paragraph (c)') to list commodities and their tolerances in parts per million. The rulemaking revises, republishes, adds table headings, revises specific commodity entries and footnotes, and may remove or add entries (e.g., removing 'Fruit, Citrus, Group 10 except Grapefruit', adding 'Tea, instant').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions include precise table-heading insertions, entry revisions, and footnote changes. Producers, registrants, and enforcement labs must refer to the updated tables for current ppm tolerances per commodity; the tables are the operative source for allowed residue levels.
